title: PandamStyle benchmark observation
description: One row of the observation stream. The first ten properties are the Benchmark Kit's required fields and are never renamed or reinterpreted; everything after them is additive. A row describes ONE metric for ONE (engine, corpus, scenario, cache state, session, iteration). It is never an aggregate: aggregation is summarize.py's job, and a harness that averaged would destroy the session structure the raw data exists to preserve.

engine.description: Which compiler, or which publication variant, produced the value. babel_current is anchored to the official hygiene baseline d5702374; babel_work_eliminated is the same compiler with the measured redundant work removed. babel_full and babel_incremental are the Spike 2 engines. The three session_* engines are the Spike 3 publication variants: the same project session, the same compilation, differing only in how the result is written to disk.

corpus.description: Corpus cell identity: c<components>-t<tokens>-r<recipes>-s<seed>. The seed is in the name because it is what makes the corpus deterministic. The optional -f<fanout> suffix is present when a cell's fanout differs from the value derived from its component count; fanout is always in the corpus manifest and the campaign metadata either way.

scenario.description: Scenario name from the protocol vocabulary. A scenario is a real content revision except where its name or kind says otherwise.

cache_state.description: The state the process was in. os_cold is not a value here: the OS page cache was never dropped, so every row is a warm-OS-cache row.

session_id.description: Independent session block. Preserved so warm events inside one session are not mistaken for independent samples.

metric.description: Metric name. The Benchmark Kit phase names are used where they exist; engine-specific sub-phases are additionally allowed, and a parse metric may be suffixed with ':<pipeline>'.

status.description: ok includes a negative case that correctly REFUSED the program: a compiler failing a build it should fail is the correct outcome, and recording it as an error would make a correct engine look broken. unsupported means the phase could not be isolated honestly; it is never a zero.

value.description: Null whenever status is not ok. There is no placeholder value: a number that was not measured is null, and the reason is in detail.

engine_variant_commit.description: The commit the engine was built from. Null when unknown, never a placeholder.

corpus_manifest_hash.description: sha256 over every generated file, path and content, in path order. Two runs are comparable only when this matches.

run_kind.description: Debug runs prove the harness and publish no performance conclusion. They are never mixed with a qualification summary.

detail.description: Why a row is ok-with-a-caveat, or why it is not ok. For unsupported metrics this carries the reason the phase could not be isolated. For parse counts it carries the most consulted module.

detail.reason: source maps are not requested by either the CLI or the adapter, so there is no source-map work to time; reporting 0 would understate the build.
